blueprint_concepts: tangents drawn from an external point to a Hyperbola
english: Let $H$ be the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^{2}}{17}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}=1$. Let $P$ be a point in the first quadrant lying on the line $2x=3y$ such that the two tangents drawn from $P$ to $H$ are perpendicular to each other. Then the slope of the tangent from $P$ to $H$ having positive slope is ______.
hindi: माना कि $H$ अतिपरवलय $\dfrac{x^{2}}{17}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ है। माना कि प्रथम चतुर्थांश में रेखा $2x=3y$ पर स्थित एक बिन्दु $P$ ऐसा है कि $P$ से $H$ पर खींची गई दोनों स्पर्श रेखाएँ परस्पर लम्बवत हैं। तब $P$ से $H$ पर खींची गई धनात्मक प्रवणता वाली स्पर्श रेखा की प्रवणता ______ है।
solution: Perpendicular tangents meet on the director circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=17-4=13$
Both give real points of contact since $17m^{2}-4>0$; positive slope $=\dfrac12$
solution_full: For $\dfrac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\dfrac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ the line $y=mx+c$ is a tangent if and only if $c^{2}=a^{2}m^{2}-b^{2}$ (with $a^{2}m^{2}-b^{2}>0$).
The locus of the point of intersection of two perpendicular tangents is the director circle $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}-b^{2}$. Here $a^{2}=17,\ b^{2}=4$, so the director circle is $x^{2}+y^{2}=13$.
$P$ lies on this circle and on $2x=3y$. Putting $y=\dfrac{2x}{3}$: $x^{2}+\dfrac{4x^{2}}{9}=13$, i.e. $\dfrac{13x^{2}}{9}=13$, so $x^{2}=9$. In the first quadrant $x=3,\ y=2$, so $P=(3,2)$.
A line through $P$ with slope $m$ is $y-2=m(x-3)$, i.e. $y=mx+(2-3m)$.
$(2m-1)(m+2)=0$, so $m=\dfrac12$ or $m=-2$. The product of the slopes is $-1$, which confirms that the two tangents are perpendicular.

For both slopes $17m^{2}-4>0$ ($\dfrac{17}{4}-4=\dfrac14$ and $68-4=64$), so each line touches $H$ at a real point: $\left(-17,-8\right)$ for $m=\dfrac12$ and $\left(\dfrac{17}{4},-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ for $m=-2$.
The tangent with positive slope has slope $\dfrac12=0.5$.

concept_use.Director circle for Hyperbola: P is located as the intersection of the director circle x^2+y^2=13 with the line 2x=3y, giving P(3,2).
concept_use.tangents drawn from an external point to: The slopes of the two tangents from P(3,2) come from (2-3m)^2 = 17m^2 - 4, i.e. 2m^2+3m-2=0, giving 1/2 and -2.

originality_note: New: the external point is fixed by two conditions (perpendicular tangents and a given line), then the tangent slopes are read from the slope quadratic (way 5). Closest known: equation of the director circle of a hyperbola; tangents from a given point. Different because: the point is not given; it must first be located on the director circle before the slope quadratic is formed.
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter introduced, conditions complete (quadrant / sign / branch stated), one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer equals the plan (decimal between 0 and 1: 0.5). Changed: No change. Checked that both slopes satisfy 17m^2-4>0 so both tangents touch H at real points, and that P is unique in the first quadrant.
key_step: Locate P on the director circle x^2+y^2=13 and the line 2x=3y, then solve the tangent-slope quadratic.
justification: Routine chain of three standard steps (director circle, intersection with a line, tangency condition c^2=a^2m^2-b^2) with no insight needed. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L2) on perpendicular tangents.
